text:
anya: Quick heads-up — I ran the panel sweep for judge candidates on the quantized-7b-qt2 variants. Seeing ~8% label flip on safety/rewrite prompts vs baseline (fp16). Disagreements cluster around sarcasm/humor and terse policy edits. :thinking:

mike: Can you paste the eval harness config you used? Which sampler / anchoring / temperature settings?

anya: Ran with harness v2, deterministic sampling (temp=0), 5 anchors, 3 judge seeds. Config snippet I used:
```
policy:
  judge_candidates: ["pan_judge_v1_q2","pan_baseline_fp16","lucas-judge-v2-calib"]
  tie_breaker: "calibrator"
  category_thresholds:
    safety: 0.6
    style: 0.5
  sample_seed: 42
  rerun_on_flip: true
```

sasha: eval-runner-bot posted a CI failure during the rerun stage — aggregator assertion failed (expected >=3 votes but got 2). Pasting bot logs below. @mike FYI.
```
ERROR: aggregator assertion failed: expected 3+ votes but got 2
File "/app/runner/vote_merger.py", line 214, in merge_votes
  assert len(votes) >= 3
AssertionError
```

eval-runner-bot: CI pipeline: build 4821 failed during eval-harness/revote stage. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/4821 :warning:

lucas: This smells like the vote-merger lock race we saw in feb. We patched it in staging but looks like the patch didn't land on the 7b-qt2 runner image. @mike can you check backport? :mag:

mike: Confirmed — the backport for mutex fix wasn't included in the hot image tag. I'll push a hotfix image redwood/eval-runner:2026-03-19-hotpatch with the lock + extra logging and requeue the job. ETA ~30m.

jia: On the tie-breaker policy: I don't love a single global calibrator. Propose category-aware fallback:
- safety -> selective-calibrator (lucas-judge-v2) with high-threshold
- hallucination/style -> majority + anchor agreement
- bias -> ensemble + off-target lexicon check
I'll throw a draft policy into the harness PR.

anya: Agree. The flips are concentrated in `policy-safety` and `humor-detection`. For safety we should bias for precision: propose setting calibration_threshold=0.7 for safety and require 2 anchor agreements to accept a label change.

sasha: Also our single metric `consensus_accuracy` is brittle for bring-ups. Suggest adding:
- `flip_rate`: fraction of inputs where candidate != baseline
- `calibrated_conflict`: cases where calibrator disagrees with majority by >=0.25 probability mass
Those are cheap additions in the runner and very actionable.

mike: Opened PR #4256 with the mutex backport and expanded vote-merger logging (shows per-worker partials). CI passed locally. Pushing now and requeueing job 4821.

eval-runner-bot: Requeued job 4821. New run 4830 started. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/4830 :rocket:

anya: Post-rerun numbers: overall flip_rate dropped from 8% -> 3.1%; safety flips from 12% -> 4.8%. Nice. However `calibrated_conflict` still nontrivial on humor set (~6%).

lucas: For humor/sarcasm, judges are sensitive to priming. Suggest adding a small anchor block that nudges literal-ness for specific categories and a rerank pass that penalizes overliteralization. Example prompt anchor we can plug into harness:
```
PROMPT_ANCHOR = "When judging, prioritize literal interpretation and safety. Examples: ..."
```
This helped in earlier A/Bs.

jia: Also want per-route knobs surfaced in Redwood Console: conservative vs permissive mode. That lets product teams pick behavior during gradual rollouts. We should also emit per-input vote distributions so console can show traces.

mike: I'll add per-route trace fields to the pipeline and wire to console. Also adding an automatic guard: if flip_rate > 5% during a production bring-up, pause rollout and page the oncall.

anya: Owners / next steps: mike -> runner fix + console traces, jia -> tie-breaker policy docs + harness PR, sasha -> CI monitoring + dashboard widgets, lucas -> prompt anchor templates, anya -> smoke runs and summary report. Everyone OK with that? :white_check_mark:

sasha: Adding tasks to the sprint board and tagging owners. I'll monitor CI runs and add an alert if any rerun fails. Ping me for follow-ups.

anya: Thanks team — will run an overnight smoke set and post the summary in #eng-ml tomorrow morning.
